mainEntity.name: How long does a dental crown typically last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dental crowns do not have a fixed lifespan, as longevity varies depending on the material used, the location of the crown in the mouth, oral hygiene standards, and individual habits such as teeth grinding. With good care and regular dental reviews, many crowns can function well for ten to fifteen years or longer. However, all crowns should be monitored over time. Only a dentist can assess whether a specific crown requires repair or replacement based on clinical examination.

mainEntity.name: Can I feel it if my crown is wearing down?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Crown wear often occurs gradually and without obvious discomfort, which is why regular dental check-ups are important. In some cases, patients may notice sensitivity to temperature or pressure, a change in how their bite feels, or visible aesthetic changes to the crown. However, significant wear can be present without noticeable symptoms. Your dentist can assess crown condition using clinical examination and, where appropriate, dental X-rays.

mainEntity.name: Will a worn crown damage the tooth underneath?

acceptedAnswer.text: A significantly worn crown may compromise its protective function, potentially allowing bacteria to access the margins of the crown and the underlying tooth. This could increase the risk of decay beneath the crown or sensitivity. In cases where the crown has worn to a degree that affects its structural integrity or seal, further assessment and management may be recommended. Individual risk varies and can only be properly evaluated through clinical examination.

mainEntity.name: Does teeth grinding always damage crowns?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bruxism — habitual teeth grinding or clenching — places higher-than-normal forces on both natural teeth and dental restorations, including crowns. Not all patients with bruxism will experience the same degree of wear; individual factors such as bite alignment, crown material, and grinding intensity all play a role. For patients with known bruxism, a custom nightguard is often recommended as a preventative measure to help protect both natural teeth and crowns from accelerated wear.

mainEntity.name: Can a worn crown be repaired rather than replaced?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends entirely on the extent and location of the wear, the condition of the underlying tooth, and the material the crown is made from. In some situations, minor surface imperfections or small chips in a porcelain crown may be smoothed or repaired using composite resin. However, where wear is more substantial or the crown margin has been compromised, replacement may be the more appropriate clinical recommendation. Only a dental professional can determine which option is suitable following a thorough examination.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal for a crown to feel different over time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some very subtle changes can occur as a crown settles in and as the surrounding gum tissue adapts. However, noticeable changes in bite sensation, comfort, or the appearance of the crown are worth mentioning to your dentist. These changes may indicate wear, a shift in bite alignment, or a separate issue with the gum tissue or underlying tooth. It is always advisable to raise any concerns with your dental team rather than assuming changes are a normal part of having a crown.
